title: Effective type, aliasing basics and object representation
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its relevant rules.
Trace the example and justify its behaviour.
Identify important assumptions and failure cases.
Apply the concept in a reviewed and tested exercise.

understand.concept: C's effective-type and aliasing rules constrain which lvalue types may be used to access an object's stored value. Character types may inspect object representation byte by byte, but arbitrary pointer casts do not make incompatible typed access valid.
understand.whyItMatters: Violating aliasing and effective-type rules can lead to undefined behaviour and surprising optimization effects, even when the memory addresses appear identical.
understand.analogy: Treat standards, interfaces and release steps as explicit contracts that make assumptions visible.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the C standard, implementation documentation or project-specific requirements.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: memcpy copies the object representation into a character array without accessing the float through an incompatible lvalue type. The byte values themselves are representation-dependent.

practise.guidedTask: Explain why memcpy is used instead of casting float * to int * and dereferencing.
practise.independentTask: Inspect an object's bytes using unsigned char and document why the representation is implementation-dependent.
hints: Character types may access an object's representation.
Do not assume a particular floating-point bit pattern on every C implementation.
Use memcpy for representation copying when appropriate.
